P, Q and R show the positions of three water particles in the wave.
Which particle has the greatest speed at the instant shown?
A
all have the same speed

hints: Look at the displacement values on the graph: P is at the peak near $3 \text{ m}$, Q is at $2 \text{ m}$, and R is at $0 \text{ m}$.
Remember each water particle moves up and down with SHM, so speed is smallest at maximum displacement and largest when passing through equilibrium.
Rank P, Q and R by how close each is to the $0 \text{ m}$ displacement line to find which must be moving fastest now.
walkthrough: The graph is displacement against distance at one instant. Read off: P is at the crest, Q is part-way down at $2 \text{ m}$, R is crossing $0 \text{ m}$ at $12 \text{ m}$ distance.
Each water particle oscillates vertically with approximately SHM. For SHM, speed $v$ is zero at the extremes and maximum at the equilibrium position.
P has maximum displacement, so its kinetic energy and speed are minimum - it is about to turn around.
Q has a large but smaller displacement than P, so it has some speed but not the maximum.
R has zero displacement, so it is passing through equilibrium where speed is greatest. This is option D.

A.explanation: Speed is not the same because each particle is at a different stage of its up-down oscillation.

B.explanation: P is at the crest with displacement about $3 \text{ m}$, so it is momentarily at rest with minimum speed.

C.explanation: Q has displacement $2 \text{ m}$ from equilibrium, so it has an intermediate speed, less than at zero displacement.

D.explanation: R is at zero displacement on the equilibrium line, where an oscillating particle has its maximum speed.
